name: Combined Immunodeficiency with Low Immunoglobulins and Normal B Cells
aliases: CID with Hypogammaglobulinemia and Normal B Lymphocytes
Combined Immunodeficiency with Normal B Cell Count

criteria.description: Serum immunoglobulin levels (IgG, IgA, and/or IgM) significantly below age-matched reference ranges
Peripheral blood B lymphocyte counts within normal limits for age
Demonstrated T-cell functional impairment by lymphocyte proliferation assays or cytokine production tests
History of recurrent, severe, or unusual infections consistent with combined immunodeficiency
Positive family history of immunodeficiency or early infant deaths from infections

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of low immunoglobulin levels, normal B cell counts, and impaired T-cell function with clinical evidence of immunodeficiency
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may aid in confirming diagnosis and identifying specific molecular defects.

pathognomonic.notes: Often affecting respiratory and gastrointestinal tracts

pathognomonic.symptomName: Normal peripheral blood B lymphocyte count
searchTerms: normal B cell numbers in blood
persistent loose stools due to germs
failure to gain weight as baby
viral infections lasting a long time

laboratory: Low serum immunoglobulin levels (IgG, IgA, IgM)
Normal peripheral blood B cell counts by flow cytometry
Impaired T-cell proliferation response to mitogens and antigens
imaging: Chest X-ray or CT showing recurrent pneumonia or bronchiectasis
genetic: Mutations in genes affecting T-cell development or function (e.g., RAG1/2, IL2RG, ADA) may be identified
Genetic heterogeneity with variable inheritance patterns

distinguishingFeatures: Absent or very low B cells
Profound T and B cell lymphopenia
Severe opportunistic infections in early infancy
Absent or very low T-cell function
Low immunoglobulins with variable B cell counts
Later onset, usually adolescence or adulthood

redFlags: Recurrent severe bacterial infections requiring hospitalization
Failure to thrive or poor growth in infancy
Persistent hypogammaglobulinemia despite normal B cell counts
references: Orange JS, et al. Use and interpretation of diagnostic vaccination in primary immunodeficiency: a working group report of the Basic and Clinical Immunology Interest Section of the American Academy of Allergy, Asthma & Immunology. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2012.

Picard C, et al. Primary Immunodeficiency Diseases: An Update on the Classification from the International Union of Immunological Societies Expert Committee for Primary Immunodeficiency. Front Immunol. 2015.
